subject: Aperture renewal: Q3 capacity proof & fallback plan
messages:
From: Claire Dawson <claire@aperturemedia.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aperture renewal conversation — throughput proof request

Jonas —

Thanks for the call earlier. Our renewal is coming up in October and procurement is pushing hard on unit-cost and latency. A competitor has proposed a migration path that promises a 30% unit-price reduction and a median tail latency improvement, and the execs have asked us to require a short, production-like proof before we finalize with Redwood.

Can you outline what a 2-week bakeoff would look like (what we need to supply, what Redwood will run, and the success criteria)? Also attach any checklist so my infra team can prep logs/traffic.

Looking to be pragmatic — Marco (cc) will coordinate the infra side.

Thanks,
Claire Dawson
Head of AI Infrastructure
Aperture Media

---
Attachment: rival-offer-summary.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dawson <claire@aperturemedia.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture renewal conversation — throughput proof request

Claire —

Appreciate the context. High-level proposal for a short proof:

- Scope: 2-week, production-shadowed bakeoff against a representative subset (~10% traffic or replay) of your live inference footprint.
- Success metrics: median latency, 95/99th latency, token cost per 1M tokens, and error-rate/response-fidelity against your golden set.
- Redwood deliverables: dedicated test pool (isolated capacity), telemetry dashboard, continuous KV/prefix caching enabled, and a runbook for the test.
- Your deliverables: sample traffic (or replay), golden prompt set (50–100 prompts), and read-only access to anonymized logs.

I attached a short checklist (redwood-benchmark-checklist.pdf) to help Marco's team get data ready. Karthik — can you add the initial capacity sizing + quoted uplift for the trial?

I'll propose dates and a canary plan once we confirm capacity.

Best,
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood-benchmark-checklist.pdf (one-page checklist)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Dawson <claire@aperturemedia.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aperture renewal conversation — capacity options for the bakeoff

Jonas / Claire —

Quick capacity note (high level):

- Option A (Hosted, burstable): 8 x V100-equivalent concurrent workers, automatic batching, approx $0.XX/token (estimated). Fast to spin up but noisy neighbors could affect tail latency.
- Option B (Dedicated pool): 4 x A100-equivalent reserved nodes, predictable 99s, lower cost per sustained throughput, we can reserve for the 2-week window and extend to a short-term uplift if you buy down the first quarter.
- Option C (Hybrid canary): Start hosted for functional checks, switch traffic to dedicated pool for 72 hours of steady-state performance capture.

I've attached a draft pricing quote for a dedicated trial (dedicated-pricing-quote.pdf). Evelyn — can you confirm we can offer a 25% trial discount and the SLA addendum for the bakeoff?

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: dedicated-pricing-quote.pdf (price table stub)

From: Claire Dawson <claire@aperturemedia.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco@aperturemedia.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture renewal conversation — capacity options for the bakeoff

Jonas / Karthik —

Thanks — this is helpful. Two points from procurement: 1) The competing vendor put the proposed renewal at 30% less TCO over 12 months and claims median latency improvements during sustained traffic. They provided a short vendor-run benchmark report (attached: rival-offer.pdf). 2) They are asking us to sign a statement of intent quickly to secure a preferred onboarding window.

We are willing to run the bakeoff, but leadership wants a clear operational fallback and a commercial counter if Redwood demonstrates parity or superior performance. Also need assurances around data handling for the trial (no model weight access, audit logs retained).

Marco will gather the golden prompts and a 48-hour sample for replay by EOD Friday.

Claire

---
Attachment: rival-offer.pdf (3-page vendor claim)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dawson <claire@aperturemedia.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture renewal conversation — capacity options for the bakeoff

Claire —

Understood. We can be very specific and time-boxed. Proposal (counter / save plan):

1) Two-week bakeoff window starting 2026-09-14 that mirrors production traffic.
2) Redwood will provide a dedicated pool (Option B) for the trial. We'll apply a 30% discount on the dedicated trial price for the two weeks, and extend that 20% discount for the first 3 months of any renewed contract if you commit to a 12-month minimum within 30 days of trial close.
3) Performance proof: we will publish a shared dashboard (redwood-hosted) with median / p95 / p99 and token-cost counters. We'll run an agreed golden-set A/B comparison and provide the raw anonymized telemetry.
4) Operational safeguards: no model weights will be shared; logs will be retained for 90 days and we will supply audit logs for the trial.
5) If Redwood cannot meet the agreed success metrics, we will provide a one-time migration credit equal to two months of committed spend, plus a fast-track onboarding slot for your preferred timeline.

Evelyn confirms SLA addendum and 25% discount for the initial trial (see attached aperture-save-offer.pdf) — this offer is valid for 10 business days.

Next steps: sign the attached trial addendum (DocuSign link below), confirm the traffic sample, and we will schedule the kickoff runbook review.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/doc/XYZ-9876
HubSpot Deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345678

Best,
Jonas

---
Attachment: aperture-save-offer.pdf (2-page save plan + SLA addendum)

From: Claire Dawson <claire@aperturemedia.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco@aperturemedia.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture renewal conversation — capacity options for the bakeoff

Jonas —

This looks fair and faster than our internal procurement timeline. Marco and I reviewed the save plan and will sign the trial addendum today so we can hit the 9/14 start.

Please schedule a kickoff for 9/13 to run the runbook and confirm telemetry hooks. Also confirm who from Redwood will own the on-call during the trial (we need a named escalation).

Claire
Head of AI Infrastructure
Aperture Media
